summary.headline: Sell focused SME workflow automation with measurable outcomes, not generic AI consulting.
summary.best_opportunity: Niche workflow automation implementation and monthly care for small UK firms
summary.why_now: Live search found BCC reporting 54% of UK firms using AI in March 2026, up from 35% in 2025, while impact on headcount remained limited. Adoption is a broad signal, not proof of local willingness to pay.

top_opportunities.name: SME workflow automation implementation and care plan
top_opportunities.description: Map one repetitive admin workflow, automate it with existing tools, document handover, and provide monthly support.
top_opportunities.why_now: BCC's March 2026 research surfaced in live search reports 54% of UK firms actively use AI versus 35% in 2025; limited headcount impact suggests adoption may not yet translate into operational gains. Validate buyer budgets directly.
top_opportunities.buyer: Small accountancy, recruitment, property and professional-service firms
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £200–£900 for software, domain, insurance deposit and outreach; validate before committing spend.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks through direct outreach and a paid audit/pilot; estimate, not guaranteed.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly monitoring, support and iterative improvements; set price after discovery.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong for a software engineer able to integrate APIs and deliver directly.
risks: SMEs may be curious but unwilling to fund implementation; test paid demand.
Data protection, reliability and ongoing support obligations need explicit controls.

scores.demand: 4/5 — adoption trend supports interest, not guaranteed buying
scores.competition: 3/5 — crowded generalist market; vertical focus helps
scores.speed_to_cash: 4/5 — service can be sold before building software

top_opportunities.verdict: Best balance of fast validation, low cost and recurring service revenue; sell one narrow outcome first.

top_opportunities.name: Lead-response and booking systems for local trades
top_opportunities.description: Install missed-call capture, web enquiry follow-up, quote reminders and booking workflows for one local trade niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: General AI adoption supports interest in practical automation, but this run found no fresh trade-specific demand evidence; validate locally before productising.
top_opportunities.buyer: Electricians, plumbers, roofers and small home-service operators
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£700 using off-the-shelf CRM, messaging and hosting tools.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–3 weeks with a demonstrable pilot and owner-led sales; estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly hosting, workflow monitoring and changes, with terms agreed per client.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong: straightforward web, CRM and API integration work.
risks: Trade operators may already use bundled CRM or answer calls personally.
Messaging consent, deliverability and lead attribution require care.
top_opportunities.verdict: Test with one trade and one measurable outcome, such as faster enquiry response.

top_opportunities.name: Local business website care and conversion improvement
top_opportunities.description: Offer a fixed-scope refresh, speed/accessibility checks, enquiry tracking and monthly maintenance.
top_opportunities.why_now: Low-cost delivery and an established recurring maintenance model make this actionable; current research gathered does not establish a new demand spike.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local service businesses with outdated sites and weak enquiry conversion
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £100–£600 for hosting, tooling, insurance and prospecting.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 1–2 weeks if sold as a paid audit followed by a scoped fix; estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly hosting, updates, analytics and bounded small changes.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Strong, especially with a focused niche and reusable templates.
risks: Price competition from DIY builders and low-cost agencies.
Clients can expect unlimited changes unless scope is explicit.

scores.demand: 3/5 — ongoing need, not evidenced as accelerating

top_opportunities.verdict: A dependable fallback service; differentiate by sector and measurable lead outcomes.

top_opportunities.name: Niche operational micro-SaaS for a repeated spreadsheet workflow
top_opportunities.description: Turn one validated, frequent spreadsheet/email process into a small paid web tool for a narrowly defined UK trade or service niche.
top_opportunities.why_now: GOV.UK and BCC digital-adoption signals support continued digitalisation but do not prove demand for a specific product. Build only after observing repeated paid workarounds.
top_opportunities.buyer: A specific small-business niche with a recurring admin bottleneck
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £300–£1,500 for hosting, APIs, basic legal needs and pilot testing if scope stays narrow.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Typically slower: 4–12+ weeks unless pre-sold; estimate.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Subscription per organisation if value and retention are demonstrated.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Very strong technically, but requires customer discovery and sales discipline.
risks: Building before securing committed users can consume budget without revenue.
Incumbents can add similar features; niche distribution is the harder problem.

scores.startup_ease: 3/5 — software feasible, support and sales less so

top_opportunities.verdict: Do not start as a standalone build; derive it from paid implementation work.

top_opportunities.name: Productized local SEO and enquiry tracking for one niche
top_opportunities.description: Provide a monthly local-search health check, landing-page improvements, review-response workflow and tracked enquiry reporting.
top_opportunities.why_now: Businesses need measurable enquiries, but live research did not establish niche-specific search demand or current pricing; validate with prospects.
top_opportunities.buyer: Local clinics, home services or independent professional practices
top_opportunities.startup_cost: £150–£800 for analytics, checking tools, landing page and outreach.
top_opportunities.speed_to_revenue: Potentially 2–4 weeks with a paid baseline audit; results take longer.
top_opportunities.recurring_revenue: Monthly retainer if reporting and improvements are valued.
top_opportunities.founder_fit: Good if paired with technical SEO, analytics and automation skills.
risks: SEO outcomes are slow and rankings cannot be guaranteed.
Crowded market and client churn if leads are not attributable.

scores.demand: 3/5 — persistent need, unverified for chosen niche

top_opportunities.verdict: Consider only with a tightly selected niche and transparent outcome reporting.

best_pick.name: SME workflow automation implementation and care plan
best_pick.why_it_wins: It monetises engineering skill without waiting for a product build, fits part-time work, and can turn successful implementations into support revenue. BCC's current adoption signal and GOV.UK SME digital-adoption work frame the opportunity, but neither guarantees buyer demand.
validation_plan: Choose one reachable vertical; interview 10 owners about a specific manual workflow, workaround, frequency and cost. Ask for a paid pilot, not hypothetical interest.
Offer a fixed-scope paid workflow audit to three prospects; proceed only if at least one pays and measurable time/error savings can be agreed.
best_pick.first_offer: A £250–£500 fixed-scope workflow audit and one automation pilot, with an optional monthly support plan; validate prices in sales conversations.
best_pick.mvp: One documented integration using the client's current CRM/email/forms, exception alerts, audit trail and human handoff; check security and lawful basis before sensitive data processing.
best_pick.do_today: Select one vertical, write a one-page offer for one repetitive process, and contact 20 local prospects for a 15-minute workflow interview.
